worked_example.problem: Which stitch would you use to fill in a leaf shape smoothly?
steps: Filling a shape needs stitches placed close together.
Satin stitch places straight stitches side by side to cover the shape.

cards.idea: Running stitch goes in and out in a line; back stitch makes a solid line.
Satin stitch fills a shape with close straight stitches.
Use an embroidery hoop to keep the fabric tight.

check.prompt: Put the steps of embroidering a design in order.

items.text: Transfer the design onto the fabric
Stretch the fabric in an embroidery hoop
Thread the needle and knot the thread
Fasten the thread neatly at the back

questions.prompt: Match each stitch to its description.

pool.right: small even stitches in and out in a line
each stitch goes back to meet the last, a solid line
close straight stitches that fill a shape

pick.q: writing a name in a solid line
finishing the edge of a blanket

questions.prompt: Put the steps of embroidering a design in order.

items.text: Transfer the design onto the fabric
Stretch the fabric in an embroidery hoop

right.text: Back stitch makes a solid line.
A hoop keeps the fabric tight.

wrong.text: Running stitch fills a shape completely.
wrong.explain: It makes a broken line; satin stitch fills.

wrong.text: Stitches should be as uneven as possible.
Never fasten the thread at the back.
wrong.explain: Fasten it neatly so it does not come undone.
